title: Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management (88 FR 37920)
publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; FDIC; OCC
limitations: Full PDF text read; due diligence factors a-n (risk management incl. SOC reports, information security incl. MFA and pen tests, operational resilience, incident reporting, physical security, subcontractors, insurance) and right-to-audit contract topic used. Guidance, not a rule; applies to banking organizations, reaches Unbound only through bank or bank-affiliated customers. [type: supervisory-guidance; access: public]

title: Proposed Third-Party Risk Management Guidance (Federal Register 2026-18859)
publisher: OCC; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; FDIC; NCUA
limitations: Only Federal Register API metadata and abstract read (risk-based alignment of TPRM to assessed risk levels). Proposal, not final; may replace or amend SRC-CAQ-001. [type: supervisory-guidance-proposal; access: public]

title: SR 24-7: FFIEC Cybersecurity Assessment Tool Sunset Statement
publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
limitations: States the FFIEC CAT was removed on 2025-08-31 and points to other resources (e.g., NIST CSF 2.0, CISA CPGs). FFIEC IT Handbook itself was not retrievable (HTTP 403) and is not used. [type: supervisory-letter; access: public]

title: SR 21-14: Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems
publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (FFIEC guidance transmittal)
limitations: Transmittal page read; underlying FFIEC guidance PDF not read in full. Addressed to financial institutions; relevant to vendors via customer expectations on MFA and privileged access. [type: supervisory-letter; access: public]

title: NYDFS Industry Letter: Guidance on Managing Risks Related to Third-Party Service Providers
publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services
limitations: Applies to Part 500 covered entities; reaches Unbound only if a customer is a covered entity (OQ-211). Contract topics used: MFA, encryption, data location, subcontractor disclosure and rejection, data use, deletion and migration at exit. [type: supervisory-guidance; access: public]

title: Regulation S-P: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information and Safeguarding Customer Information (final rule, FR 2024-11116)
limitations: Only Federal Register API abstract read (incident response programs, customer notification, service provider oversight). SEC fact sheet returned HTTP 403. Applies to broker-dealers, advisers and similar; reaches Unbound only via such customers. 72-hour service provider notice figure taken from echelon-due-diligence research, not re-verified here.

title: Truist Third Party Information Security Specifications V5.2
limitations: Requirement document for Truist suppliers, not a fill-in questionnaire; contract terms prevail. Used for SSO federation, 24-hour deprovisioning and notice, subcontractor notice, testing expectations. Strictest-case example; DAF sponsors likely ask less. [type: bank-supplier-requirements; access: public]

title: Morgan Stanley Minimum Security Standards
limitations: Supplier standard aligned to NIST; used for independent pen testing, production data in lower environments, AI use, patching. Applicability to Morgan Stanley GIFT vendors is inferred, not stated. [type: bank-supplier-requirements; access: public]

title: STAR Level 1: Security Questionnaire (CAIQ v4.1)
limitations: Landing page read; questionnaire workbook not downloaded or read here. CAIQ is published by CSA for public use; question text not reproduced. Domain mapping relies on CCM domain names. [type: industry-questionnaire; access: public page; download offered with or without account]

title: Vendor Security Alliance questionnaire (VSA CORE 2027 and VSA FULL 2027)
limitations: Only the public landing page was read: free with registration, licence limited to assessing own vendors and excludes consulting or hosted vendor-management use; CORE up to 122 and FULL up to 278 questions across 21 sections (incl. AI, tenant isolation, sub-processors and exit, assurance). Questionnaire content not seen. [type: industry-questionnaire; access: registration required; licensed]

title: SIG 2026: Key Updates and Considerations
limitations: SIG is licensed; sharedassessments.org returned a sign-in interstitial. Only this licensee summary was read (Lite/Core/Detail presets, ISO 42001 AI mapping, operational resilience, no new domains in 2026). No SIG question text seen or used. [type: secondary-summary-of-licensed-framework; access: public blog; SIG itself licensed by Shared Assessments]

title: At-Bay Cyber Insurance Application (AB-CYB-APP, Ed. 06.2026)
limitations: Full text extracted. Asks about the applicant's own enterprise (MFA, offline and immutable backups, EDR product, phishing training, payment controls). Relevance to customer questionnaires is indirect. [type: insurance-application; access: public]

title: Beazley Ransomware Supplemental Application (05/2022 edition)
limitations: Full text extracted; 2022 edition may not reflect current underwriting. Used for PAM, EDR, end-of-life software, phishing simulation, backup questions. [type: insurance-application; access: public]

title: Tokio Marine HCC NetGuard Plus and MEDEFENSE Plus Application
publication_date: 2026 (glossary marked 2026; exact edition date not confirmed)
limitations: Full text extracted. Used for EDR coverage percentage, MFA for local and remote privileged access, and call-back verification questions. [type: insurance-application; access: public]

title: Indiana Cyber Insurance Toolkit: Underwriting Security Controls Questions and Resources
publisher: State of Indiana, Indiana Cybersecurity Hub
limitations: Compilation of typical underwriting questions (MFA for privileged access, EDR on all endpoints, continuous monitoring, workstation firewalls) by a state government, not an insurer form. [type: government-guidance-on-insurer-questions; access: public]

title: SOC 2 - SOC for Service Organizations: Trust Services Criteria
publication_date: not stated (page lists 2026-11-16 exposure drafts of proposed 2027 TSC)
limitations: Overview page only; Trust Services Criteria text not read (see echelon-assurance OQ-100). [type: professional-standard-overview; access: public page; criteria PDF requires account]

title: SOC 1 - SOC for Service Organizations: ICFR
limitations: Overview page: SOC 1 covers controls likely relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting. Relevant to sponsors whose auditors rely on Unbound ledgers. [type: professional-standard-overview; access: public]

title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
limitations: Publication landing page read; framework body not re-read. Used as the reference framework banks may cite after the FFIEC CAT sunset. [type: framework; access: public]

title: SOC 2 Reports and Penetration Tests
publisher: Cloud Security Alliance (republished from MJD; author Mike DeKock, CPA)
limitations: Practitioner opinion: SOC 2 does not explicitly require a pen test, but customer contracts often do. Not authoritative. [type: practitioner-commentary; access: public]

title: Our Security Practices
limitations: Sponsor's own donor guidance (log in only through the sponsor site, avoid giving credentials to third-party tools). Not a vendor requirement; implies a product constraint (inferred). [type: daf-sponsor-public-statement; access: public]

title: 3rd Party / Vendor BCP Questionnaire
limitations: Short university form; used for recovery objectives, loss-of-resource strategies and 12-month actual-recovery exercise questions. Not a financial-sector form. [type: customer-questionnaire; access: public]

title: Real-world questionnaire and customer expectation research (DD-QNR-001)
limitations: Secondary: summarizes 63 public sources retrieved by another agent on 2026-11-25; claims not re-verified here except where a SRC-CAQ public source is also cited. [type: internal-research; access: internal repository (read locally)]

title: DAF sponsor technology procurement profile (DD-IND-DAF-001)
limitations: No DAF sponsor or community foundation publishes a vendor questionnaire; DAF-sponsor expectations are largely inferred from parent-company supplier documents and privacy notices. [type: internal-research; access: internal repository (read locally)]

title: Agentic controls and sponsor audits research queue (peer assurance posture table)
limitations: Records public trust-center claims of DAF and grantmaking software peers (SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, pen testing statements). Peer claims are self-reported marketing statements. [type: internal-research; access: internal repository (read locally)]
